# HBC+ Home Battery Master Switch v1.2 - how this flow works

Part of **HBC+ v1.2** (Home Battery Control Plus), with the phase guard for two batteries per phase. HBC+ settings live in `packages/hbc_phase_guard.yaml` and on the **Phases** view of the HBC+ dashboard.

Decides **who controls the Marsteks**, from `input_select.marstek_master_battery_mode`. Runs when that helper changes and periodically (*Check work modes periodically*), and loops over M1 ... M*n* (`input_number.house_battery_count`).

| Master mode | RS485 control | Work mode | Who controls |
|---|---|---|---|
| Full control | enable | unchanged | HBC+ (forcible charge / discharge) |
| Marstek control | disable | unchanged (choose it in the Marstek app) | Marstek firmware |
| Manual control | disable | manual | Marstek firmware, manual mode |

*Set RS485 and Work Modes* builds the `select.select_option` actions per battery; *Set RS485* and *Set work mode* perform them.

## HBC+ v1.0 - two batteries per phase

The phase rules only act when `input_select.house_battery_phase_guard_mode` is **Enforce**. On **Off** and **Monitor** this flow works without phase rules.

When control goes back to the firmware (RS485 *disable*), two batteries on one phase could each run at full power under their own firmware and overload the phase fuse. On **Enforce**, only the battery with the lowest M-number on a shared phase is handed back. Its partner gets RS485 *enable* plus forcible *stop*, so it stays idle even when Node-RED is down; the node status turns yellow for that battery. Batteries alone on their phase, and all batteries on Off / Monitor, are handled exactly as before.

The Home Assistant fallback for a stale HBC+ heartbeat (`packages/hbc_heartbeat.yaml`) applies the same rule: on Enforce only the lowest M-number per shared phase goes back to firmware, its partner stays RS485 *enable* + forcible *stop*.

While `binary_sensor.hbc_heartbeat_stale` is on, the periodic check skips *Full control* (*Skip while HBC heartbeat is stale*): switching RS485 back on would undo that fallback, and a battery would resume the last forcible command in its registers with no control loop running. *HBC heartbeat back* re-applies the master mode as soon as the heartbeat is fresh again. A change of the master mode itself is always applied.

Fail-open: if the phase check fails, the battery is handled as before and a warning is logged.

Applies a **PID preset** to the Self-consumption controller when `input_select.house_battery_control_pid_presets` changes. The preset is written to five helpers that the Self-consumption flow reads:

| Preset | Kp | Ki | Kd | Input smoothing | Output smoothing |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Very safe | 0.1 | 0.1 | 0 | 0 % | 10 % |
| Safe | 0.3 | 0.3 | 0.1 | 20 % | 0 % |
| Regular | 0.3 | 0.4 | 0.8 | 50 % | 10 % |

Helpers: `input_number.house_battery_control_kp`, `_ki`, `_kd`, `_error_signal_dampening` (input smoothing) and `_pid_output_dampening` (output smoothing). Any other option leaves the values unchanged, so manual tuning survives.

No change. On Enforce the PID output is spread over fewer batteries per phase (one active battery, within the fuse room), but the control loop and its tuning are the same.

# HBC+ Home Battery Start v1.2

Part of **HBC+ v1.2** (Home Battery Control Plus). This tab is the control loop: every other tab works through it.

## What it does, each tick
1. **Trigger** - a P1 measurement starts the cycle; the rate is limited so the batteries are never flooded with writes.
2. **Read** - *Read HA states (fast)* reads the batteries (`marstek_mN_*`) and the P1 meter.
3. **Totals** - *Batteries (totals)* sums SoC, power and energy over all batteries and computes the per-phase planner ceilings (see below).
4. **Strategy** - the strategy selected through the *Strategy arbiter* calculates the desired battery power.
5. **Phase guard** - limits each battery so the fuse of its phase is never overloaded (Off / Monitor / Enforce).
6. **Set Batteries** - writes the setpoints to the Marsteks.
7. **Heartbeat** - publishes that the loop works: only after a good cycle (the strategy returned without an error, and at least one battery was written without an error).

## Details
- **Battery totals guard** - an `unavailable`/`unknown` battery value never becomes NaN. Per battery and value: a valid number is used and remembered; a missing one uses that battery's last good value for up to 5 min; after that the battery adds 0 to the totals. The strategies get the same held values, and a battery without a usable SoC or power limit for more than 5 min gets limits of 0 W and `data_ok = false`, so it is not driven. Node status: green OK, yellow holding, red counted as 0 (battery and value named); a warning is logged only when that state changes.
- **Phase planner** - on *Enforce* the ceiling per phase follows a moving average (15 min) of the house load on that phase, rounded to 100 W with 250 W hysteresis, so strategies plan with the room that is really there.
- **Set Batteries** - writes are awaited, one cycle at a time (*Write limiter*, with coalescing); a value only counts as sent after the write succeeded (*Collect completions*); *write errors* are caught with a 30 s stale-lock failsafe; *Write latency* feeds the rate limiter. The mode is written only on change after a successful write, when HA's read-back disagrees for 20 s, or as a 60 s keep-alive; only the power register in use is written (none in *stop*); power is written before the mode, through one *Write (awaited)* node. Every solution is validated first (mode stop / charge / discharge, power a number, clamped to 0 ... max; otherwise *stop*), and nothing is written to a battery whose RS485 is off (its firmware is in control).
- **Heartbeat** - *HBC+ heartbeat (max every 60 s)* publishes `hbc/heartbeat` (retained ISO time) -> `sensor.hbc_last_run` (`packages/hbc_heartbeat.yaml`). It is fed from the end of a cycle (*Write latency* and *solutions present*, through the link *HBC+ cycle result*), so it stops when the strategy fails on every tick or every battery write fails. When it is older than 5 min while `input_select.marstek_master_battery_mode` is *Full control*, Home Assistant hands the batteries back to their firmware (phase-aware) and notifies; the Master Switch flow re-enables RS485 only once the heartbeat is fresh again.
- **Logger and health** - *Custom logger* always counts warnings and errors and writes them to the Node-RED log (the same message at most once a minute), also with Insight mode off. *HBC+ health* publishes `hbc/health` (retained JSON) -> `sensor.hbc_health` (ok / warning / error, with the last error) when it changes.
- The battery strategy (`input_select.house_battery_strategy`) is changed by other flows only through the *Strategy arbiter* tab.

More: `docs/user-guide.en.md` in the repository (https://github.com/CodeRubbere/HASS-HBC-Plus).

# HBC+ Home Battery Start v1.2 - how this flow works

Part of **HBC+ v1.2** (Home Battery Control Plus), with the phase guard for two batteries per phase. HBC+ settings live in `packages/hbc_phase_guard.yaml` and on the **Phases** view of the HBC+ dashboard.

The control loop of HBC+. On every P1 update (rate limited) it reads the batteries and the settings, runs the selected strategy, and writes one setpoint per battery to the Marsteks.

## One control tick

1. **Start / Rate limiter** - triggered by `sensor.p1_meter_power`. *Operational thresholds* switches between a fast and a power-saving rate, based on how much the grid power changes and how long the last strategy run and battery write took.
2. **Read HA states (fast)** - reads every battery (M1 ... M*n*, `input_number.house_battery_count`) and the HBC+ settings in one node, from the Home Assistant states in global context (server option *Expose to global context*). Falls back to the original chain of current-state nodes when those states are not available.
3. **Batteries (totals)** - total battery power, max charge / discharge power and usable energy. Written (on change) to the `input_number.house_battery_total_*` helpers. A value that is briefly unavailable is held for up to 5 min; the strategies get the held value too. A battery without a usable SoC or power limit for more than 5 min is not driven (limits 0 W, `data_ok = false`).
4. **Update battery order** - rotates the battery priority (`input_number.house_battery_control_prioritize_battery`, `input_select.house_battery_control_priority_change_interval`).
5. **HBC+ phase planner** - new, see below.
6. **Strategy selection** - `input_select.house_battery_strategy`, or the EV stop trigger strategy while `sensor.ev_is_charging` is on. A dynamic link call runs the strategy tab whose link-in has that name. The strategy returns `msg.solutions`: one `{id, mode, power}` per battery (mode `charge` / `discharge` / `stop`).
7. **solutions present -> HBC+ phase guard -> Write limiter** - the guard is new, see below. *Write limiter* allows one write cycle at a time and keeps only the newest setpoints while a cycle is in flight.
8. **Set Batteries** - per battery: power first, then mode, each only when it changed, when Home Assistant's read-back differs for more than 20 s, or (mode) as a 60 s keep-alive. Writes are awaited; *Collect completions* marks a value as sent only after success; *Write latency* feeds the rate limiter. Each solution is validated first (mode, power a number, 0 ... max; otherwise *stop*), and a battery with RS485 off (firmware in control) gets no writes.

Also on this tab: the **HBC+ heartbeat** (`hbc/heartbeat` at most every 60 s and only after a good cycle -> `sensor.hbc_last_run`; Home Assistant hands the batteries back to their firmware when it goes stale), **HBC+ health** (`hbc/health` -> `sensor.hbc_health`: warnings and errors of the last 10 minutes), the debug dashboard and logger (warnings and errors always reach the Node-RED log, also with Insight mode off), insight mode, peak shave settings and the unhandled-exception handling.

## HBC+ v1.0 - two batteries per phase

The phase rules only act when `input_select.house_battery_phase_guard_mode` is **Enforce**. On **Off** and **Monitor** this flow works without phase rules.

- **HBC+ phase planner** (between *Update battery order* and *Strategy selection*). Off: the msg passes untouched. Monitor / Enforce: adds `msg.phase_plus` with, per phase L1-L3 that has batteries:
  - the **room** for charging and discharging: min(grid fuse - margin -/+ house net, battery circuit - margin), where house net = P1 phase power minus the battery power on that phase;
  - the **active battery** per direction: *SoC balance* (charge the emptiest, discharge the fullest, swap only after the SoC delta **and** the minimum dwell), *Fixed order* or *Rotate daily*; with *Shared headroom* every battery that can serve the direction is active;
  - **break-before-make**: a newly chosen battery stays blocked while the previous one still runs above 100 W, or has no data.
- **Strategies** use `msg.phase_plus` only on Enforce: *Load distribution* (Self-consumption) and *Max power solution* (Charge, Sell).
- **HBC+ phase guard** (between *solutions present* and *Write limiter*): last check of `msg.solutions`. Enforce: a battery that is not active on its phase goes to idle (1 W, relay stays engaged) and the total per phase and direction is trimmed to the fuse room; corrections go to the debug board. Monitor: the node status shows `would: ...` and nothing changes. The last result is in global `hbcplus_guard_last`.
- **Batteries (totals)**: on Enforce the max charge / discharge power is counted per phase - one battery (or the shared room) capped at battery circuit - margin and at the room the house leaves under the grid fuse (house load per phase averaged over ~15 min, rounded to 100 W, changed only by >= 250 W) - plus the own-circuit batteries. Charge Deadline plans with that value (a future HELIOS integration would too).
- **Errors**: the planner, the guard and the totals addition run in try/catch. On Off / Monitor an error passes the msg on unchanged. On **Enforce** it is fail-safe: *Set Batteries* then applies the strict rule (per shared phase only the lowest M-number runs, at most battery circuit - margin). Home Assistant also switches to *Full stop* when a phase stays overloaded (`hbc_phase_guard.yaml`). The Home Assistant alarm `binary_sensor.hbc_phase_limit_exceeded` works independently of Node-RED.
- Signs: battery power > 0 = charging; P1 phase power > 0 = import.

## HBC+ v1.2 - price guard

The price guard swaps the strategy that is about to run while prices are negative. Settings and price state come from `packages/hbc_price_guard.yaml` (Timed/Dynamic view); it is **Off** by default.

- **Read HA states (fast)** also reads `sensor.hbc_price_state`, `input_select.house_battery_price_guard_mode` and `binary_sensor.hbc_phase_shared`. They are optional: a missing one means no price guard, never the fallback to the old read chain.
- **Strategy selection** builds `msg.price_override` = `{mode, state, map, reason}` once per tick and applies it to the top-level strategy, after the EV stop trigger. The msg carries it into every strategy tab, so Dynamic, Timed, Charge and Sell apply the same map without depending on another tab.
- **Map.** `export_negative` (feeding in costs money): *Sell* -> *Charge PV*, *Zero import* -> *Self-consumption*, *Standby / peak shave* -> *Charge PV*. `import_negative` (you are paid to import): every strategy except *Full stop* -> *Charge*, with the goal forced to *batteries are full*.
- **Safety.** *On* only with the tariff source *Grid Clock*; *Full stop* is never changed; no override while the EV stop trigger is on; `import_negative` only on phase guard *Enforce* or with no shared phase; a missing `msg.price_override` or entity means no change (fail-open).
- **Monitor** changes nothing; the nodes that would change the strategy show `would: <from> -> <to>` in their status.
- **HBC+ price guard status** fires the HA event `hbc_price_guard_status` when the outcome changes; it feeds `sensor.hbc_price_guard` and the Home view card.

# HBC+ Strategy Charge v1.2 - how this flow works

Part of **HBC+ v1.2** (Home Battery Control Plus), with the phase guard for two batteries per phase. HBC+ settings live in `packages/hbc_phase_guard.yaml` and on the **Phases** view of the HBC+ dashboard.

Charges the batteries from the grid **until a goal is reached**, then hands over to the *goal reached* strategy.

## Goal (`input_select.house_battery_strategy_charge_goal`)

| Goal | Reached when |
|---|---|
| batteries are full | every battery is at its max SoC, or the energy is at about 99.9 % of the max |
| state of charge | the average SoC reaches `input_number.house_battery_strategy_charge_target_soc` |
| energy reserve | usable energy reaches `input_number.house_battery_strategy_charge_target_energy` |
| solar forecast | usable energy reaches the max energy minus today's expected PV surplus (`sensor.solar_forecast_today` minus `input_number.house_battery_solar_reserved_for_house`) |
| anything else | not recognised -> Full stop |

`input_boolean.house_battery_strategy_charge_goal_reached` shows whether the goal is reached; once it is, the strategy in `input_select.house_battery_strategy_charge_goal_reached` runs (default *Charge PV*).

## Power

- **Import limit on** (`input_boolean.house_battery_control_has_power_limit_import`): *Regulated power* - Self-consumption is driven to grid import = the import limit, with discharging disabled. A feed-forward start jumps straight to the expected power for 10 s, then the PID trims the rest.
- **No import limit**: *Max power solution* - every battery at its max charge power.

## HBC+ v1.0 - two batteries per phase

The phase rules only act when `input_select.house_battery_phase_guard_mode` is **Enforce**. On **Off** and **Monitor** this flow works without phase rules.

- *Max power solution*: on a shared phase only the active battery (by default the one with the lowest SoC) charges, at min(its max, the phase's fuse room). Its partner idles at 1 W. A battery alone on its phase is still capped at the fuse room, which takes the house load on that phase into account.
- *Regulated power* goes through Self-consumption, which applies the same rules.

## HBC+ v1.2 - price guard

- *Set reached strategy* applies the price guard (`msg.price_override`, see the Start tab) to the follow-up strategy after the goal is reached.
- **Price goal** (new, between *Goal* and *Charge until*): with `import_negative` and the guard **On**, the goal is forced to *batteries are full*, so a negative import price fills the batteries completely. On *Monitor* only the status shows it.

# Charge Deadline - HBC+ v1.1

Part of **HBC+ v1.2** (Home Battery Control Plus). Based on Charge Deadline v2.1; the
logic is unchanged, the phase guard section below says how it works with two batteries
per phase.

## HBC+ v1.0 - two batteries per phase

Nothing in this tab's logic changed for HBC+ v1.0. It works with the phase guard through
the values and sub-strategies it already uses:

- **Max charge power.** `msg.batteries_max_charge_power` (and
  `input_number.house_battery_total_max_charge_power`, used by the dashboard estimates)
  come from *Batteries (totals)* in **HBC+ Home Battery Start v1.1**. With the phase guard
  on **Enforce** that is counted per phase: one battery per phase (or the shared room),
  capped at battery circuit - margin and the room the house leaves under the grid fuse. So the cheap-hours-enough test and the plan count on the
  power that can really flow (3 x 2500 = 7500 W, not 15 000 W with six batteries).
  On Off / Monitor it is the plain sum, exactly as before.
- **Execution.** `charge` mode hands over to Self-consumption; its *Load distribution*
  (HBC+ Strategy Self-consumption v1.1) gives the power only to the active battery on each
  phase and never more than that phase's fuse room. The fallback strategies in
  `idle` / `hold` / `fallback` go through the same phase guard.
- **When the fuse room binds** (house load on a phase while charging), the batteries charge
  less than planned in that tick. A load that lasts (heat pump) also lowers the max charge
  power HBC+ reports (averaged over ~15 min), so the plan books extra cheap quarters for it. The plan is recomputed from the remaining energy and time
  every tick, with `PLAN_HEADROOM` 0.90 and the 15-minute end buffer, so it catches up later.
- Status *at import limit* is the house-level grid import limit. The per-phase fuse limit is
  shown on the **Phases** view of the HBC+ dashboard (charge room per phase), not here.

---

## History: what v2 changed on v1

- **Price-weighted pacing** (Cheapest hours only). Each cheap quarter gets a weight
  `w = 1 + (ratio - 1) * (pHi - price) / (pHi - pLo)`; the remaining energy is shared in
  proportion to `w x minutes`, so the cheapest quarter charges `ratio` times as hard as the
  priciest cheap quarter and the total still lands on the target by the deadline.
  `ratio` = `input_number.house_battery_deadline_price_ratio` (1-5; 1 = flat = v1).
  `pLo`/`pHi` come from ALL of today's cheap quarters, so weights never shift as quarters
  pass and the per-tick re-plan is stable. Per-quarter prices arrive via
  `sensor.deadline_window.quarters` (from `sensor.deadline_cheap_blocks.quarters`).
- **Import-limit-aware plan.** Every quarter is capped at
  `min(pack limit, import limit - smoothed house net load)` and water-filled (the 150 W
  margin was removed 2026-10-16); the
  same cap feeds the cheap-hours-enough test and the PV-reservation feasibility. Status
  says *at import limit* when the grid, not the packs, is binding.
- **Plan projection for the dashboard** (2026-10-30). With weighting on, the power in a
  pricier cheap quarter is low *on purpose*, so the dashboard's estimate rows - which
  extrapolated the current power over every block - read "short" while the plan was on
  track. `Compute plan` now also sums what the weighted plan places in the cheap quarters
  **after** the current one (`msg.deadline.plan_energy`, kWh; -1 when no weighted plan is
  running) and the `Planned energy` node writes it to
  `input_number.house_battery_deadline_planned_energy`. `sensor.deadline_estimated_soc` and
  `sensor.deadline_charged_at` then use: rest of this quarter at the MEASURED power + that
  planned energy, so a lagging PID still shows as short. Computed in `charge` (weighted
  branch) and in `idle` (waiting for cheap hours). At -1 the rows behave as before.
- **Planning margin (v2.1, 2026-10-31).** Pacing to land *exactly* on the deadline left no
  slack: charge losses, the packs tapering near full, or the house load rising in a later
  block made it end short while the import limit still had room (Dynamic-Charge, at full
  power, did reach 100 %). `Compute plan` now:
  - plans the AC energy `needWh = shortfall / CHARGE_EFF` (`CHARGE_EFF = 0.92`); the
    shortfall itself (`remaining_energy`, the latch) stays battery-side;
  - plans against `PLAN_HEADROOM = 0.90` x the cap (cheap-hours-enough test, weighted plan,
    PV feasibility). The live command is still clamped at the FULL cap (`nowCapW`), and a
    weighted plan that saturates the planning cap goes straight to the full cap;
  - aims to finish `END_BUFFER_MIN = 15` minutes early: the flat average divides by
    `max(1, minutes - 15)`, the weighted plan drops the last 15 minutes of quarters
    (`trimTail`, never the current one). Not applied to the gap-overflow case.
  - `plan_energy` for the dashboard is converted back to battery-side (x `CHARGE_EFF`).
  Tune the three constants at the top of `Compute plan`.
- **One tab only:** every Charge Deadline version exposes the link-in `Charge Deadline`.
  HBC+ ships only this one; never enable an older v1/v2 tab next to it.

---


Charge the batteries to a target **before a deadline**, as cheaply as the window allows,
without taking over the battery control loop. The actual battery command is always delegated
to an existing sub-strategy; this tab only decides *how much grid power to ask for*.

Runs on **every P1 update (up to ~1 Hz)** via the `Charge Deadline` link-in, dispatched by the
**HBC+ Home Battery Start v1.1** flow when `input_select.house_battery_strategy` is set to
*Charge Deadline*.

---

## Layout

| Group | Runs | Does |
|---|---|---|
| **Configuration** | every tick | link-in, breadcrumb trace |
| **Settings (off the control path)** | on change + every 30 s | one `render_template` call -> `flow.deadline_cfg` |
| **Compute plan** | every tick | decides the mode and the grid setpoint |
| **Delegate to sub-strategy** | every tick | hands the msg to Self-consumption or the fallback |
| **UI / analytics** | at most every 10 s | writes the helpers the dashboard reads |
| **Unhandled exceptions** | on error | red node status, returns to the caller |

The control path is `link in -> Trace -> Compute plan -> Mode -> (Regulated charge \| Idle) ->
Run sub-strategy -> End`. It performs **no entity lookups**: every setting comes from flow
context. An earlier version walked seven `api-current-state` nodes in series on every tick to
fetch values that change only when someone touches a dashboard.

## Settings cache

`Render settings` asks Home Assistant for one JSON blob (goal, targets, fallback, both
booleans, the PV forecast, and `sensor.deadline_window`'s attributes) and `Cache settings`
stores it in `flow.deadline_cfg` with a `stamp`.

* A failed render **keeps the previous snapshot** - one bad refresh is harmless.
* `Compute plan` treats a snapshot older than **5 minutes** as no settings at all and falls
  back, rather than commanding a charge from settings that may no longer be true. It warns at
  most once a minute while that lasts.
* Because Home Assistant computes `in_window` and `now_hms`, this flow never parses a clock
  time, so the Node-RED container's timezone cannot shift the window.

## Modes (`msg.deadline.mode`)

| Mode | When | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `charge` | inside the window, energy still needed | Self-consumption PID driven to `grid_target`, discharge disabled |
| `idle` | *Cheapest hours* pacing, waiting for the next cheap period | fallback strategy, discharge allowed - anything used now is re-bought cheaply |
| `hold` | target reached and *hold* is on | fallback strategy but discharge stays disabled, so the reserve survives to the deadline |
| `fallback` | outside the window, unconfigured, or stale settings | fallback strategy, nothing held |

**Target reached is latched**, keyed on window + goal, and cleared when the window closes.
Without the latch the fallback discharges the moment the target is met, the shortfall crosses
the tolerance again, and the next tick re-buys the same energy - a ping-pong that runs for the
rest of the window. With *hold* off the latch becomes 0.30 kWh of hysteresis instead.

## The plan

```
need_W     = energy_still_needed / CHARGE_EFF                    (v2.1: AC side)
required_W = need_W / max(1, charge_time_left - END_BUFFER_MIN)  (v2.1: finish 15 min early)
grid_target = clamp(required_W - measured_PV_surplus, 0, pack_limit, import_limit)
```

Planning (the cheap-hours-enough test, the weighted plan, PV feasibility) uses
`PLAN_HEADROOM` x the cap; the commanded power may still use the full cap.

* `charge_time_left` is the sum of the periods that can still be charged in - every cheap
  period under **Cheapest hours** (all of them, not just enough to cover the energy), every
  Charge Deadline period still ahead under **Time slot**. Only a manual window paces on the
  wall clock, because there every minute to the deadline is a minute it may charge in.
  Under Timed the gaps between periods are dead minutes: the Timed strategy does not
  dispatch Charge Deadline in them, so pacing across them would under-charge inside the
  periods and dump the catch-up on the last one.
* If the cheap periods cannot carry it in time (2026-10-16 behaviour): inside a cheap block
  the plan charges at the cap (*cheap hours too short, max power*); in a gap it buys only the
  overflow the blocks cannot take, spread over the gap minutes left. Price weighting is off
  in that case - at the cap there is nothing to weight.
* `reserve_pv` subtracts today's forecast surplus so a sunny afternoon is not pre-empted by
  morning grid charging - and switches itself off once the job barely fits at full power.
* Recomputed from the *remaining* energy and time every tick, so it self-corrects: more sun
  means less grid next tick.

## Message contract

**Reads** (put on the msg by HBC+ Home Battery Start v1.1 - never looked up here):
`batteries[]`, `batteries_total_power`, `batteries_max_charge_power`,
`batteries_available_energy`, `grid_power`, `grid_power_has_limit_import`,
`grid_power_limit_import`. With the phase guard on Enforce, `batteries_max_charge_power` is
the per-phase value (see HBC+ v1.0 above) and the msg also carries `phase_plus`, which this
tab does not read.

**Sets:** `msg.target` (the sub-strategy to run), `msg.house_target_grid_consumption_in_w`,
`advanced_settings.discharge_disabled`, `strategy.display`, and `msg.deadline.*` for the UI.

## UI writes

`Write when changed` quantises before comparing (25 W, 0.05 kWh) and rate-limits to 10 s.
The slow gate writes required power, remaining energy/minutes, status and the planned
energy (projection above); the fast gate (1 s) writes the PV / grid / shortage bar.
Without the quantisation the status string moved on nearly every tick and the gate never
matched - about 5 000 service calls an hour, all of them recorded. In practice it now writes
roughly once a minute while charging.

## What lives in Home Assistant, not here

The window, the cheap periods and everything the dashboard shows are template entities in
`hbc_deadline_charge.yaml`: `sensor.deadline_cheap_blocks` merges adjacent price
marks into runs, `sensor.deadline_window` derives the window from them (or from the two
`input_datetime` helpers under *Manual window*), and `sensor.deadline_pacing` decides which
of the two it is from the active strategy. Those are deliberately **not** written by this
flow: a helper written from Node-RED freezes at its last value the moment another strategy
takes over.

## Failure behaviour

Every path below ends in the fallback strategy, never in an uncommanded charge: no settings
yet, stale settings, no window configured, no goal configured, no batteries on the msg,
malformed price blocks, or an unreadable clock.

# HBC+ Strategy Dynamic v1.2 - how this flow works

The Start flow calls this tab on **every P1 update** (link in `Dynamic` / `Dynamic 2`).
That fast path does **not** read the period selectors: it runs whatever strategy is cached
in `flow.dynamic_strategy` (via *Has strategy* -> *Set strategy* -> *Sub-strategy*).
An empty cache means **Full stop** (*Set Full stop*).

`flow.dynamic_strategy` is recalculated only by the **Update when** group:

| Trigger | When |
|---|---|
| *Update strat* | every 15 min (and once, 3 s after deploy) |
| *Clear cache* / *Midnight* | 00:01, 13:15 and 15:00 - also re-fetches the prices |
| *User input* | any change of the entities below |

*User input* watches:

- `input_select.house_battery_strategy` (master strategy)
- `input_select.house_battery_strategy_dynamic_data_source`
- `input_number.house_battery_strategy_dynamic_threshold_delta`
- `input_number.house_battery_strategy_dynamic_cheapest_hrs`
- `input_number.house_battery_strategy_dynamic_expensive_hrs`
- `input_select.house_battery_strategy_dynamic_default` - **Baseline / regular period** *(local)*
- `input_select.house_battery_strategy_dynamic_cheapest` - **cheapest period** *(local)*
- `input_select.house_battery_strategy_dynamic_expensive` - **expensive period** *(local)*

## Period selectors in *User input* (HBC+)

The three period selectors marked *(local)* are part of *User input*, so a change to the
regular, cheapest or expensive period recalculates the strategy within a second or two
(prices come from the cache, so no extra API call). Without this, such a change would only take
effect at the next quarter-hour tick.
## Still forces Full stop

`flow.dynamic_strategy` is empty - and the batteries go to **Full stop** whatever the
selectors say - when:

- the tariff data source is *None* (*Set dynamic strategy to null*),
- Node-RED just restarted and no recalculation has run yet.

No price data is **not** a reason for Full stop: *Determine dynamic strategy* then runs the baseline
strategy and shows *No price data* (see *When the price source fails*).

## API call to Data Source = link-call section (HBC+ v1.0, 2026-11-14)

*API call to Data Source* is a subroutine. *Cache check* calls it on a cache miss with the
**link call** node *Fetch from Data Source* (static, timeout 30 s). The section fetches and
converts the prices, caches them (*Cache data source*) and ends in **Return to caller**
(link out, mode *return*). The link call then passes the msg, with `msg.dynamic` filled, to
*to Determine Strategy*, exactly like a cache hit.

Replaces the earlier hand-off by plain link out and the *Called via Link Call?* switch
(`msg._linkSource`) with *link out 12*. Other tabs can call the section the same way
(see below). A failed fetch, or an error inside the section, still ends in *Return to caller*
(see *When the price source fails*), so the link call does not wait for its timeout.

### Calling it from another flow

Add a **link call** node with a timeout >= 30 s, in one of two ways:

- *static*: pick *Dynamic Fetch from Data Source*; pick it again after a re-import of this tab with new node ids;
- *dynamic*: set `msg.target = "Dynamic Fetch from Data Source"`; keeps working after a re-import. Not on a msg
  HBC+ uses for control (inside a strategy tab), because there `msg.target` names the strategy.

The tab *HBC+ Example: price fetch* (`node-red/examples/price-fetch-example.json`) shows the dynamic way.

*Prepare request* (first node of the section) fills in what the caller leaves out:

| msg property | In / out | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `dynamic.data_source` | in, optional | price source; default = `input_select.house_battery_strategy_dynamic_data_source` (read from global HA states) |
| `dynamic_use_cache` | in, optional | `true` = return this tab's cached prices if still valid (same rule as *Cache check*), else fetch |
| `dynamic` | out | `{data_source, data_all: {list, list_marked, average, min, max, start, ...}, no_data?}` |
| `dynamic_from_cache` | out | `true` when the cache answered |
| `dynamic.stale` | out | `true` when the source failed and the last valid prices of that source came back |
| `target` | in, optional | only for a dynamic link call: `"Dynamic Fetch from Data Source"` |

Source *None* or unreadable returns at once with `dynamic.no_data = true` and an empty list,
so the caller never waits for the timeout. A successful fetch also refreshes this tab's cache.
The rest of the caller's msg comes back unchanged (`msg.template` is used and removed).

### When the price source fails (HBC+ v1.0)

- **Last valid prices kept.** *Cache data source* keeps the cached list when a fetch fails, as long as
  it is from the same source and still covers the current interval; it goes on with `dynamic.stale = true`
  and the next run tries the source again.
- **Errors caught.** An error inside *API call to Data Source* (for example the template render while
  HA is disconnected, or a macro error) goes through *Catch fetch errors* and *Fetch error* to *Cache data source*
  and is handled like a fetch without prices. *Fetch error* logs it as a warning and shows it in its status; an
  error inside *Cache data source* itself goes straight back to the caller.
- **Fallback.** With no valid prices at all, *Determine dynamic strategy* runs the baseline strategy
  (*Default to*) instead of the last one, and publishes `status: no_data`.
- **Alert.** `sensor.hbc_energy_prices_data` carries `status` (ok / stale / no_data);
  `binary_sensor.hbc_price_data_missing` turns on, the dashboard shows a warning, and after 30 min
  HA sends a notification (`hbc_control.yaml`).
- **Pinned sensor.** `input_text.house_battery_strategy_dynamic_price_sensor` names the price sensor for
  sources that otherwise rely on auto-detection; *Data source settings* shows in its status which sensor is used.

## HBC+ v1.2 - Grid Clock feed, buy and sell prices, price guard

- **Grid Clock** (tariff source, the Grid Clock feed). *Data source settings* sends it to its second output, past the Cheapest Energy Hours macro: *Grid Clock feed request* builds `v1/hbc/{zone}/{slug}/latest.json` from `input_select.house_battery_gridclock_zone` and `input_text.house_battery_gridclock_provider_slug` (`market` without a supplier) -> *Grid Clock feed* (http request, `If-None-Match`, a `304` reuses the cached file) -> *Grid Clock feed parse*. The parse builds `data_all.list` (buy) and `data_all.sell` in the format the macro path delivers, adds the chosen BE grid operator's ct/kWh to the buy price (and to the sell price only where sell = buy), and fires `hbc_gridclock_status` -> `sensor.hbc_grid_clock_feed`. A failed fetch keeps the last valid prices, as with every source. The tab environment variable `GRIDCLOCK_FEED_URL` points to the feed (default `https://cdn.gridclock.eu/v1/hbc`). *Grid Clock* no longer uses the Grid Clock integration.
- **Group *Grid Clock suppliers*.** Loads `v1/hbc/{zone}/index.json` at start, daily at 00:10, when the zone changes and after every (re)connect to Home Assistant (*HA (re)started*), and fills the supplier and grid-operator selects. The choice is kept in `input_text.house_battery_gridclock_provider_slug` and `..._grid_operator_name`, because HA forgets runtime select options after a restart. *Index request* waits for HA's states and never guesses a zone; *Index apply* ignores an index of a zone that is no longer selected.
- **Price split** (before *Cache data source*, so the cache and every link-call caller get it): every source gets a sell list; without the feed sell = buy.
- **Determine dynamic strategy.** Every mark carries `sell` and `neg` (`import` / `export` / null). The HIGH side of a pair is valued at the sell price when *Strategy during expensive period* is *Sell*, otherwise at the buy price, which runs the v1.1 code unchanged. With separate sell prices the pairing uses two lists (lows by buy, highs by sell), each quarter once, and stops when the best remaining pair no longer clears *Minimum spread*.
- **Selected** applies the price guard (see the Start tab) to the strategy before *Sub-strategy* runs it.

# HBC+ Strategy Partials v1.2 - how this flow works

Part of **HBC+ v1.2** (Home Battery Control Plus), with the phase guard for two batteries per phase. HBC+ settings live in `packages/hbc_phase_guard.yaml` and on the **Phases** view of the HBC+ dashboard.

Three small strategies that all run **Self-consumption** with one direction switched off:

| Strategy (link-in) | Self-consumption with | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Charge PV | discharging disabled | charges only from PV surplus, never discharges |
| Zero import | charging disabled | discharges to keep grid import at 0 W, never charges |
| Standby / peak shave | charging and discharging disabled | batteries idle (soft stop, no relay clicks) |

**Peak shaving**: when grid power exceeds the import or export limit set in HBC+, *Mode selection* switches to peak shaving and the batteries are used to stay below the limit. It persists while the batteries are still needed (*Peak check*) and ends by a time-out once they are not.

## HBC+ v1.0

No change in this tab. Everything runs through Self-consumption, which applies the phase rules on Enforce.

# HBC+ Strategy Self-consumption v1.2 - how this flow works

Part of **HBC+ v1.2** (Home Battery Control Plus), with the phase guard for two batteries per phase. HBC+ settings live in `packages/hbc_phase_guard.yaml` and on the **Phases** view of the HBC+ dashboard.

The **PID controller** of HBC+. It keeps grid power at a target - 0 W by default, or the target a calling strategy sets in `msg.house_target_grid_consumption_in_w` - by charging or discharging the batteries. Most strategies use it as their executor: Charge and Sell (regulated), Partials (Charge PV, Zero import, Standby / peak shave), Charge Deadline, and the sub-strategies of Dynamic and Timed.

## How it runs

1. **Inputs / Pre processing** - grid power, the target, and the caller's `advanced_settings` (`charge_disabled`, `discharge_disabled`).
2. **PID step** - error = grid power - target; 15 W deadband; P, I and D terms with the gains from the PID helpers (see *HBC+ Home Battery PID presets*), input and output smoothing, anti-windup on the available battery power. Settings are cached in flow context (refreshed from Home Assistant at most every 10 min, or on change). *Bumpless operation* keeps the I-term and D-term smooth when Ki or the target changes.
3. **Load distribution** - spreads the PID output over the batteries in priority order, each up to its own max. A limit or PID output that is not a number counts as 0 W, so one battery without data no longer blocks the others. Near full the charge power is limited (1500 W from 95 %, 1000 W from 99 %). A battery that is not needed keeps 1 W (relay engaged) and is stopped only after the idle time. Batteries at their SoC limits, with RS485 not enabled, or whose direction is disabled by the caller are soft-stopped. Returns `msg.solutions` and the PID load figures.

## HBC+ v1.0 - two batteries per phase

The phase rules only act when `input_select.house_battery_phase_guard_mode` is **Enforce**. On **Off** and **Monitor** this flow works without phase rules.

In *Load distribution*, on Enforce:
- a battery that is not the active one on its shared phase is soft-stopped like a battery at its SoC limit (log: `HBC+ phase standby on Lx`);
- the power given to the batteries of a phase never exceeds that phase's fuse room for the current direction (log: `HBC+ fuse room Lx ... W`);
- the anti-windup uses this capped capacity, so the I-term does not wind up when the fuse room is the limit.

# HBC+ Strategy Sell v1.2 - how this flow works

Part of **HBC+ v1.2** (Home Battery Control Plus), with the phase guard for two batteries per phase. HBC+ settings live in `packages/hbc_phase_guard.yaml` and on the **Phases** view of the HBC+ dashboard.

Discharges the batteries to the grid **until a goal is reached**, then hands over to the *goal reached* strategy.

## Goal (`input_select.house_battery_strategy_sell_goal`)

| Goal | Reached when |
|---|---|
| batteries are empty | usable energy is 0 kWh (all batteries at their min SoC) |
| state of charge | the average SoC drops to `input_number.house_battery_strategy_sell_target_soc` |
| energy reserve | usable energy drops to `input_number.house_battery_strategy_sell_target_energy` |
| anything else | not recognised -> Full stop |

When the goal is reached, the strategy in `input_select.house_battery_strategy_sell_goal_reached` runs (default *Charge PV*).

## Power

- **Export limit on** (`input_boolean.house_battery_control_has_power_limit_export`): *Regulated power* - Self-consumption is driven to grid export = the export limit, with charging disabled.
- **No export limit**: *Max power solution* - every battery at its max discharge power.

## HBC+ v1.0 - two batteries per phase

The phase rules only act when `input_select.house_battery_phase_guard_mode` is **Enforce**. On **Off** and **Monitor** this flow works without phase rules.

- *Max power solution*: on a shared phase only the active battery (by default the one with the highest SoC) discharges, at min(its max, the phase's discharge room). Its partner idles at 1 W. The discharge room shrinks when PV is already exporting on that phase.
- *Regulated power* goes through Self-consumption, which applies the same rules.

## HBC+ v1.2 - price guard

*Strategy after reached* applies the price guard (`msg.price_override`, see the Start tab) to the follow-up strategy after the sell goal is reached. *Sell* itself is swapped to *Charge PV* by the caller (Start, Dynamic or Timed) while exporting costs money.

# HBC+ Strategy Timed v1.2 - how this flow works

Part of **HBC+ v1.2** (Home Battery Control Plus), with the phase guard for two batteries per phase. HBC+ settings live in `packages/hbc_phase_guard.yaml` and on the **Phases** view of the HBC+ dashboard.

Runs a **different strategy per time period**. Period A is always on; B to E are switched on with `input_boolean.house_battery_strategy_timed_has_period_b` ... `_e` (each only when the previous one is on). Times come from `input_datetime.house_battery_strategy_timed_period_a1` / `_a2` ... `_e1` / `_e2`, the strategy per period from `input_select.house_battery_strategy_timed_strat_a` ... `_e`, and outside all periods the baseline `input_select.house_battery_strategy_timed_strat_0` runs.

## How it runs

- **Timed settings cache** - one snapshot of all periods in flow context, refreshed when a period helper changes and every 30 s.
- **Pick period** (every P1 update) - the first enabled period whose window contains *now* wins; a window is [start, end), and an end before the start runs past midnight. *Now* is Home Assistant's local time, so the container's timezone cannot shift the periods. Without a fresh snapshot (> 5 min old) it falls back to the original read chain.
- **Execute sub-strategy** - dynamic link call to the chosen strategy. The selected period is shown in `input_text.house_battery_strategy_timed_period_selected` (written when it changes, and every 10 min as a repair).

## HBC+ v1.0

No change. The strategy it runs applies the phase rules on Enforce.

## HBC+ v1.2 - price guard

*Pick period* applies the price guard (`msg.price_override`, see the Start tab) to the strategy of the chosen period. On *Monitor* it only shows `would: ...` in its status.

info:
# Battery Oscillation Guard

Watches the power of every battery (`sensor.marstek_m1_battery_power` … `m6`; batteries you don't have never trigger) and detects when the batteries swing
between **charging and discharging at high power** repeatedly (a wave).

When detected:
1. Asks 'Strategy arbiter' to **hold Full stop** (*Request: hold Full stop*, link call
   'Strategy request'). The guard has the highest priority there.
2. After `STOP_S` seconds (default 300 = 5 min) it sends a **release** (*Request: release*).
   The arbiter restores the strategy that was active before - or keeps a manual change made
   during the pause, or a hold of another flow that is still running.
3. Ignores new detections for `GRACE_S` seconds so the batteries can settle

The release is always sent at the end of a pause, also when local state was lost.

## Tuning (tab Environment variables - double-click the tab)
- `THRESHOLD_W` - a battery counts as charging above +T W, discharging below -T W (hysteresis between)
- `WINDOW_S` / `MIN_FLIPS` - trigger when one battery flips charge<->discharge >= MIN_FLIPS times within WINDOW_S
- `STOP_S` - how long to stay in Full stop
- `GRACE_S` - quiet period after restoring
- `DRY_RUN` - true = only detect + log, don't change strategy

## Notes
- Every trigger is written to the HA Logbook.
- A phone notification (with date/time) is sent on Full stop and on restore
  via `script.hbc_notify` (set where it goes on the Advanced settings view of the dashboard).
- The strategy is no longer written here: 'Full stop' and the restore are requests to
  'Strategy arbiter' (hold / release). The arbiter keeps its state in HA, so a
  Node-RED restart during the pause no longer leaves the strategy on Full stop
  (the 'On deploy' inject sends a release).

# HBC+ Phase monitor v1.2 - how this flow works

Part of **HBC+ v1.2** (Home Battery Control Plus), with the phase guard for two batteries per phase. HBC+ settings live in `packages/hbc_phase_guard.yaml` and on the **Phases** view of the HBC+ dashboard.

**Read-only.** Shows on the HBC+ dashboard what the phase guard does (Enforce) or would do (Monitor). It writes nothing to any battery and is not part of the control loop: disabling this tab has no effect on HBC+.

## How it runs

- Every 5 s, *Phase planner (monitor)* reads from the Home Assistant states in global context: the phase settings, the phase of each battery (`input_select.marstek_mN_phase`), each battery's SoC, power, RS485 mode and limits, and the P1 power per phase.
- Per phase it works out the direction (charging, discharging or idle, from the measured battery power), the charge and discharge room under the grid fuse and the battery circuit, which battery would be active and why, and where the batteries differ from the phase rules (`would`), for example `limit L1 to 2200 W (now 2327 W)`.
- It publishes over MQTT (retained), via the *mqtt.publish* action:
  - `hbc/phase/L1` ... `L3` -> `sensor.hbc_phase_l1_active` ... `l3` (state = active battery, attributes standby, mode, room, setpoint, would, reason, since);
  - `hbc/phase/summary` -> `sensor.hbc_phase_findings` (number of phases where HBC+ would act).
- A topic is republished when its content changes, and at most every 30 s otherwise.

## Monitor tab vs. the guard in the loop

This tab uses the **measured** battery power. The *HBC+ phase planner* and *HBC+ phase guard* nodes in *HBC+ Home Battery Start v1.1* use the setpoints HBC+ is about to write. On Enforce, those nodes do the actual limiting; this tab then shows the result. Small differences between the two are normal (a few seconds of battery response time).

Guard mode Off: publishes `guard off` once and does nothing else.

# Strategy arbiter

The only flow that writes `input_select.house_battery_strategy`.

Other flows **request** a strategy with a *link call* to **Strategy request**:
`msg.arbiter = {requester, action: 'hold' | 'release', strategy, reason}`; `requester` is any name, e.g. `'guard'` or the name of your own flow

- Priority: oscillation guard (100) > any other requester (50) > your own choice (base). Equal priority: the hold that came first wins.
- Effective strategy = highest active hold, otherwise the base.
- A manual change wins: it becomes the base and marks running holds as overridden; they are not re-applied until released.
- Release puts back the next hold or the base.
- The reply carries `msg.arbiter_result` / `msg.strategy_action` for the caller's log.
- State is mirrored to `input_text.hbc_strategy_arbiter` (package `hbc_strategy_arbiter.yaml`) and restored on start.
- Every change is written to the HA logbook.

Any requester name works and gets priority 50. To give one another priority, add it to `PRIO` in *Arbitrate*.
